questions.prompt: Which taught meaning of 热 fits this context?
questions.context: After being active in warm weather, the speaker feels uncomfortably warm.

choices.label: The speaker is warming an object up.
choices.feedback: 热 describes a high temperature or a person feeling hot. Here it describes a state rather than an action of warming something up.

choices.label: The speaker feels cold.
choices.feedback: 热 describes a high temperature or a person feeling hot. Here it describes a state rather than an action of warming something up.

choices.label: The speaker feels hot.

Familiar meanings available: person; people; big; large.

rubric.text: I named the distinguishing visible stroke or position.
I did not count recognition as a completed handwriting attempt.
I described the additional horizontal stroke in big rather than giving only an English meaning.
I attempted the separately assigned person writing part; its writing result stays separate from these choices.

questions.prompt: You need a teacher’s attention and then a peer’s help. Give a familiar suitable address for each; if you miss the reply, use the taught repetition request.
questions.context:
You first need your teacher’s attention, then a peer’s attention. Each helps you. Thank them. You miss the peer’s next reply; use the already taught repetition-request chunk and wait.
Familiar meanings available: you, used respectfully; you; teacher; thank you; please say it once more.
questions.label: Take your speaking turn

rubric.text: My address fits the named relationship.
I used a repetition request for a missed reply rather than as a general greeting.

definition.summary: Your results distinguish checked answers from self-reviewed practice. Unsampled material and unassessed proficiency remain separate.
